description: Conserved-meaning dimensions used by invariants.json. Each dimension is a tiny, explicit, language-neutral extractor: apply the patterns to a piece of delivered text and read off a value. It is deliberately NOT a general NLP model — it only has to be exact on the vectors that cite it, and small enough that any platform can reimplement it in a few dozen lines.

matching.regex_flavour: ECMA-262 subset: literals, character classes, alternation, \b word boundaries
matching.scalar_rule: values are tested in the order listed; the FIRST value with any matching pattern wins; if none match, `default` is the value
matching.set_rule: every value with any matching pattern is collected; the result is a set

polarity.description: Is the proposition asserted or denied? The single highest-consequence distinction in a clinical or interview note: 'did' versus 'did not'.

certainty.description: Is the claim hedged or committed? Erasing a hedge upgrades a guess to a fact, which is a fabrication the reader cannot detect.

time.description: When did it happen? 'in pain now' and 'in pain yesterday' are different clinical facts.

actor.description: Who did it, or who it was done to. Losing or swapping the actor reassigns an act to the wrong person.

quantity.description: Numeric values present, normalised to digits so 'fifteen' and '15' are the same reading. Only the numbers the vectors actually use are listed — this lexicon grows with the cases, never speculatively.

unit.description: Units of measure. A dose that keeps its number and loses its unit is more dangerous than one that loses both, because it still looks complete.

request_or_refusal.description: Is this a report, an instruction, or a refusal? 'stop the infusion' and 'do not stop the infusion' are opposite instructions built from the same words.

correction_marker.description: The word that tells a reader the NEXT value supersedes the previous one. Delete it and 'fifty, sorry, fifteen' becomes a list of two doses instead of a correction. Deliberately excludes the self-correction triggers ('scratch that', 'no wait') that the disfluency filter is SUPPOSED to consume along with the text they retract.

assessment.description: A judgement expressed about something ('the dose is right'). Tracked separately from polarity because 'not right' needs BOTH to survive to keep its meaning.
